review.name: Château Tanunda
review.reason: For: grand 1890 chateau open daily with 40-min cellar tours and croquet lawn; Wikivoyage and southaustralia.com list it. Against: both list it as a winery/cellar door, which the rules exclude unless a recognised attraction.
review.judge_objection: For: grand 1890 chateau open daily with 40-min cellar tours and croquet lawn; Wikivoyage and southaustralia.com list it. Against: both list it as a winery/cellar door, which the rules exclude unless a recognised attraction.

review.name: Jacob's Creek Visitor Centre
review.reason: For: barossa.com and Wikivoyage list it; self-guided Trail of Discovery creek walk and demonstration vineyard make a 30+ min stop at a famous brand. Against: it is a cellar door/visitor centre of a winery.
review.judge_objection: For: barossa.com and Wikivoyage list it; self-guided Trail of Discovery creek walk and demonstration vineyard make a 30+ min stop at a famous brand. Against: it is a cellar door/visitor centre of a winery.

review.name: Louden Brae School
review.reason: For: tourism-board listing of a restored 1905 one-teacher schoolhouse, famed as R.M. Williams' school. Against: single source, a stone building with a short visit, and the page gives no open-to-public detail (directions via the visitor outlet), so interior access is unconfirmed.
review.judge_objection: For: tourism-board listing of a restored 1905 one-teacher schoolhouse, famed as R.M. Williams' school. Against: single source, a stone building with a short visit, and the page gives no open-to-public detail (directions via the visitor outlet), so interior access is unconfirmed.

review.name: R.M. Williams Story (Jamestown)
review.reason: For: tourism-board listing of an outdoor interpretive display on the R.M. Williams brand founder, born near Jamestown, in Robinson Park (free, always accessible). Against: single source, an outdoor panel display likely 15 minutes, close in theme to the Louden Brae School and the museum's R.M. Williams exhibit.
review.judge_objection: For: tourism-board listing of an outdoor interpretive display on the R.M. Williams brand founder, born near Jamestown, in Robinson Park (free, always accessible). Against: single source, an outdoor panel display likely 15 minutes, close in theme to the Louden Brae School and the museum's R.M. Williams exhibit.
